title: Do Prediction Markets Forecast Cryptocurrency Volatility? Evidence from Kalshi Macro Contracts
hypothesis: Daily absolute volume-weighted probability changes in Kalshi macro prediction markets forecast 5-day ahead cryptocurrency realized volatility beyond HAR and market controls, with channel specificity: Fed/policy -> BTC, CPI -> altcoins
data_sources: Kalshi public API closing prices volumes open interest
CoinGecko daily closing prices BTC ETH SOL ADA AVAX LINK
CBOE VIX S&P500 DXY Fed Funds futures 10y Treasury Deribit DVOL BLS release calendar
sample: Ten Kalshi event series (KXFED KXCPI KXCPICORE KXGDP KXU3 KXPCECORE KXRECSSNBER KXACPI KXRATECUT KXUSNFP) and six cryptocurrency assets (BTC ETH SOL ADA AVAX LINK). Merged calendar dataset January 2023 to March 2026 with N=1183 calendar days. Weekends and US holidays excluded dropping approximately 30 percent of calendar days. Effective after 1-day lag and merging with crypto returns 193 to 569 observations per series. Estimation samples: BTC Fed-dovish M3 N=318, CPI M3 N=264 per asset, KXRECSSNBER usable N=569, descriptive per asset N=1178.
method: 1. For each Kalshi series s and day t aggregate multiple contracts j: Delta_vw_s_t = sum(V_jt * Delta_p_jt)/sum(V_jt) equation 1. Primary signal = |Delta_vw_s_t|. Directional Fed-dovish = -Delta_vw_KXFED. Directional CPI/NFP analogous. Alternatives: 5-day EMA of lagged signal and cross-sectional composite averaging across active series.

2. Crypto log returns r_a_t = ln(P_at/P_a_t-1). Dependent variable 5-day forward realized volatility RVol_a_t_h5 = sqrt(252)*sd(r_a_t+1...r_a_t+5) equation 2. Robustness: 1-day |r_t+1|, GARCH(1,1) conditional variance, log(RVol+0.001), 21-day RVol. Calendar scaling note sqrt(365/252)=1.20.

3. HAR benchmark M1: RVol = alpha + beta1|r_t-1| + beta2 mean|r|_5 + beta3 mean|r|_20 + e. M2 adds Ctrl=(VIX_t, r_DXY, r_SP500). M3 adds Kalshi_s_t-1 one-day lagged. Gap >=21h: Kalshi 4pm ET, crypto midnight UTC 7pm ET, dependent starts t+1. Controls aligned 4pm ET.

4. Inference: overlapping 5-day RVol uses Newey-West HAC 5 lags. Non-overlapping 5-day windows uses HC3. Multiple testing 60 signal-by-asset combinations Benjamini-Hochberg FDR q=0.05. Block moving-block bootstrap block length 5 with 2000 resamples.

5. Controls and orthogonalization: project Fed-dovish onto Fed Funds implied rate change + |change| + VIX + DXY + SP500 first-stage R2 2.3pct, residual t=3.62. Project KXCPI onto 10y Treasury return + VIX + DXY + SP500 first-stage R2 7.5pct residuals t=-2.29 ETH -2.79 SOL -2.60 ADA -3.73 LINK.

6. Out-of-sample expanding window initial 120 obs. Compute MSFE ratio M3/M2 and OOS R2 vs expanding historical mean. Clark-West nested statistic f_t = e_b^2 - [e_a^2 - (yhat_b - yhat_a)^2] one-sided. CSSED = sum(e_b^2 - e_a^2). Horizon profile h=1,3,5,10 with HAC lags=min(h,5) robustness h=21. Lead-lag placebo compares lag t-1 vs lead t+1.

7. Baseline comparisons: substitute lagged Fed Funds implied rate change M_FF t=-0.83 and 10y Treasury return M_UST t=+0.01 and joint with Kalshi Fed t=+3.45 p<0.001; ETH Treasury t=-0.25 joint Kalshi t=-2.10 p=0.035. Joint with Deribit DVOL level: BTC Kalshi t=+3.46 p=0.001 DVOL t=+1.58 p=0.12 ETH Kalshi t=-2.08 p=0.037 DVOL t=-1.52 p=0.13. Release-window dummy 3-day BLS and non-release subsample checks.
